en.headline: Two media outlets receive suspicious letters containing white powder from UK
en.dek: Police and specialist teams responded after staff at HK01 and Ta Kung Wen Wei Media Group found powder believed to be crushed oatmeal in airmail letters.
body: Hong Kong police are investigating after two media organisations received suspicious letters containing white powder on Wednesday.

Police said staff at the Kwai Chung office of online outlet HK01 opened an airmail letter from the United Kingdom at around 3pm and discovered the powder inside. Officers from the Explosive Ordnance Disposal Bureau, the Fire Services Department’s hazardous materials team and the Counter Terrorism Response Unit were deployed to the scene.

Later the same evening, staff at an office of the Ta Kung Wen Wei Media Group in Aberdeen reported receiving a similar letter. Both cases have been classified as seeking police assistance pending further tests and inquiries.
Authorities said the powder was believed to be crushed oatmeal. No injuries were reported, and investigations into the source and motive continue.

zh.headline: 兩傳媒機構同日收英國寄出白色粉末信 警展開調查
zh.dek: 《香港01》葵涌辦公室及大公文匯傳媒集團香港仔辦事處先後接獲內藏粉末的空郵信件，警方派員到場處理。
body: 警方周三接獲兩宗傳媒機構收到可疑信件的報告。下午約3時，《香港01》葵涌永得利廣場辦公室職員打開一封由英國空郵寄出的信件，發現內藏白色粉末後報警。
爆炸品處理課、消防處危害物質專隊及反恐特勤隊隨即到場。傍晚，大公文匯傳媒集團位於香港仔田灣的辦公室亦收到類似信件。
警方表示，粉末相信是壓碎的燕麥片。兩宗案件暫列「求警協助」，正調查寄件人及動機，目前無人受傷。
有關機構已疏散受影響員工，辦公室運作大致回復正常。
